notes:
ACCESS: article.com reached DIRECTLY over IPv4 (HTTP 200) with probe.py/curl_cffi - no proxy needed, matching the prior Home-Decor pass. robots.txt names no Claude/anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot agent and allows /browse/; only /checkout, /order, /api, /account, /search? and /discount are disallowed, none of which I touched. The origin rate-limits bursts with HTTP 429, so all fetches were serialised with backoff and every 429 was retried to a 200.

TREE SOURCE: /category_sitemap.xml is STALE and must not be used on its own - it still lists dead nodes and old IDs. The authoritative tree is the full mega-menu JSON, which Article server-renders into every /browse page inside the Nuxt payload under the key "navigation" (nested id/url/name/items). I extracted that array by balanced-bracket scan from /browse/1/sofas and used it as the spine. Article publishes TWO parallel taxonomies over the same leaf URLs: a room taxonomy ("Rooms": Living Room / Bedroom / Dining & Kitchen / Home Office / Entryway / Outdoor) and a product-type taxonomy ("Products": Seating / Tables / Beds & Bedroom / Storage & Organization / Outdoor / Rugs, Lighting & Decor). Per the brief's PRIMARY PRODUCT TYPE > ROOM NAME priority I used the product-type spine, which covers every furniture leaf exactly once and avoids the heavy duplication the room spine would produce (e.g. Bookcases & Shelving appears in Living Room, Home Office, Entryway and Storage). The room parents were fetched only as a cross-check and all resolve to supersets of leaves already captured: Living Room 600, Dining & Kitchen 193, Home Office 88, Entryway 65 items.

URL SHAPE TRAP: /browse/<id>/<slug> is routed by the SLUG, not the id. The same id serves different categories under different slugs - /browse/702/all-tables is 346 items but /browse/702/file-cabinets is 6; /browse/104/outdoor-dining is 110 but /browse/104/outdoor-sets is 113; /browse/17 serves sofas-ottomans (98), outdoor-ottoman-and-pouf (11) and floor-lamps. So the ids in the prior Home-Decor pass do not conflict with these - both are correct. Every URL below was fetched individually and its h1 confirmed to match the category name claimed.

QTY METHOD: every qty is the rendered listing header - Article server-renders exactly one "N items" string per listing, inside the Sort & Filter block. I confirmed by targeted extraction that the string inside the 'Sort & Filter' container is the only "N items" occurrence on the page, so the value is unambiguous. No structured/API source was used and none was needed. I did NOT count product hrefs - as the brief warns, rendered /product/ links are polluted by recommendation carousels (e.g. /browse/87/swivel-chairs reports 34 items but renders 110 distinct product hrefs).

SANITY CHECKS RUN: (1) All 39 leaf counts were fetched a SECOND time in a separate pass and all 39 matched exactly with no redirect - zero drift. (2) Counts vary per URL across the full range 6..154, so no value is a site-wide total. (3) Partition checks: Dining Chairs & Stools parent (155) = Dining Chairs & Seating 117 + Stools 38 EXACTLY; All Tables parent (346) vs children 116+63+66+13+10+46+26 = 340, a 6-item remainder; All Bedroom parent (283) vs 121+36+43+54+25+mattresses 10 = 289; Outdoor Dining parent (110) vs 69+27+12 = 108. These near-exact reconciliations confirm the child sets are complete. (4) h1 checked on every page to catch silent parent-serving; the only silent redirects found were dead legacy slugs (below). (5) No suspiciously round or capped numbers.

DEAD / LEGACY URLS EXCLUDED (all verified by fetch): /browse/103/sofas-daybeds 301s to /browse (All Products, 1839) - there is no separate daybeds category, daybeds live inside Beds; /browse/113/outdoor-benches 301s to /browse/61/outdoor-dining-chairs; /browse/79/tables-counter-bar-tables 301s to /browse/10/tables-dining-tables; /browse/90/tables-consoles-carts 301s to /browse/72/tables-consoles; /browse/26/decor-accents 301s to /browse/48/decor. Two legacy pages are still live but appear nowhere in the current nav and are superseded, so they were excluded to avoid duplicate rows: /browse/16/bedroom-dressers "Dressers & Nightstands" (75) is the old combined node now split into Dressers & Armoires (43) + Nightstands (36), and /browse/114/storage-benches-ottomans "Storage Benches" (33) is subsumed by Storage Beds & Benches (59). /browse/3/tables (346) and /browse/5/chairs (359) are legacy umbrella aliases of All Tables and the Seating group.

GROUPING ROWS: Seating, Tables, Beds & Bedroom, Storage & Organization, Outdoor Lounging and Outdoor Dining all have extractable children, so per the hierarchy rule they carry qty=null/link=null even though the site does publish a number for each (All Seating 727, All Tables 346, All Bedroom 283, Storage & Organization 220, Outdoor Lounging 409, Outdoor Dining 110). Article nests two further intermediate parents inside Seating - "Sofas, Sectionals, & Loveseats" (/browse/1/sofas, 407 items, parent of Sofas & Loveseats / Sectionals / Sofa Beds / Modular Seating) and "Dining Chairs & Stools" (/browse/431/chairs-dining-chairs-stools, 155 items, parent of Dining Chairs & Seating 117 + Stools 38, summing EXACTLY). Because the workbook has only Category + Sub-Category columns, a third nesting level in one column would make the reading order ambiguous, so those two intermediate parents were flattened away and their leaves sit directly under Seating; their own totals are recorded here instead. Outdoor Sets (113) is emitted as a LEAF, not a group: its only nav children are ?tc= filter query-strings, which the brief forbids recording. It is also a SIBLING of Outdoor Lounging and Outdoor Dining rather than a child of either (it spans both lounge sets and dining sets), so in reading order it is placed before both grouping rows, directly under the Outdoor Furniture category. Noted anomaly: the Outdoor department page /browse/58/outdoor reports 401 items while its own child Outdoor Lounging reports 409 - a genuine, reproducible inconsistency in Article's own counts (both re-read and stable). It affects no emitted qty because both are parents and neither is a grouping row I assigned a number to.

OVERLAP FLAGS: Article's taxonomy cross-lists rather than partitions. I ran a product-ID intersection test on the suspicious pairs and flagged four leaves that overlap a broader sibling rather than subdividing it: Swivel Chairs (all 34 inside Lounge Chairs), Dining Banquettes & Benches (36 of 37 inside Benches), Bedroom Benches (21 of 25 inside Benches), and Storage Cabinets (essentially all inside Sideboards & Cabinets). They are kept because each is a first-class, separately shoppable node in Article's live navigation with its own URL, h1 and exact count - but they must not be summed with their broader siblings. Storage Beds & Benches (59) was tested the same way and is genuinely distinct (only 20 items shared with Beds), so it is unflagged.

EXCLUDED AS NOT FURNITURE: Mattresses (/browse/60/bedroom-mattresses, 10) - bedding, not furniture, and Article splits it cleanly from Beds so no combined-node exception was needed. Bedding & Inserts, Pillows & Throws, Rugs & Runners, Performance Rugs, Outdoor Rugs, Rug Pads - textiles. Lighting and its four children, and Mirrors - out of scope here and already captured by the Lighting and Wall Decor passes. Planters & Pots, Outdoor Accessories & Decor (102), Umbrellas & Stands, Furniture Covers, Cushion Cover Sets - decor and furniture care/parts. Decor > Poufs (/browse/65/decor-poufs) was excluded as a decor node, but Seating > Ottomans & Poufs (/browse/17/sofas-ottomans, 98) IS included because Article files it under the Products > Seating department, which is exactly the condition the brief sets for poufs. Wall Shelves (/browse/52/wall-shelves, 15) excluded: Article files it under Decor > "Mirrors, Shelves & Planters" alongside mirrors and planters, which is the decorative wall-shelf case the brief assigns to Wall Decor, not the freestanding-shelving case - freestanding units are covered by Bookcases & Shelving (80). Also dropped as §3 navigation junk: New Arrivals, Best Sellers, Sale, all /c/collections* landing pages, Furniture Bundles, Shop By Material, Contract Grade, Ideas & Inspiration, Article Pro, and every ?tc=/?av= filter query-string link in the mega-menu.
